arguments.content:
validator-fix-2 (F2)

Compact review of fix/val-doc-1…task/validator-fix-2 · head d61aee5 · 7 files · +137/−10

TL;DR

The patch fixes a cross-chain block-number mix-up on routed Vea deployments. For Arbitrum→Gnosis, Sepolia is the L1/router used to prove Arbitrum finality, while the Vea outbox is on Chiado. A Sepolia finalized block number must therefore never be used as a Chiado blockTag.

The code now keeps those provider roles separate: Arbitrum finality uses the router/L1 provider; outbox contract reads and log ranges use the outbox chain provider; Arbitrum message status uses the router/L1 provider. The watcher supplies both. The validator challenge path avoids fetching an outbox-chain finalized block it never consumes.

Compatibility: routes where the outbox is itself on L1 continue to work through veaRouterProvider ?? veaOutboxProvider and the optional outbox-chain-provider fallback.

What changed, by file

validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.ts

resolveSettledReadBlocks gains outboxChainProvider. The tuple returned by getBlocksAndCheckFinality is renamed locally from outboxFinalized to l1Finalized, making its actual role explicit. After Arbitrum/L1 finality and the epoch boundary pass, the function obtains the outbox’s own finalized head when a distinct provider was supplied.

const outboxFinalized = outboxChainProvider
  ? await outboxChainProvider.getBlock("finalized")
  : l1Finalized;

return {
  inboxBlock: inboxFinalized.number,
  outboxBlock: outboxFinalized.number,
};

Why: on Arbitrum→Gnosis, l1Finalized.number belongs to Sepolia, whereas outbox reads belong to Chiado. The fallback preserves the Arbitrum→Ethereum case, where those roles share a chain.

validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.ts

The claim flow now passes two providers into makeClaim: queryRpc for Arbitrum finality (veaRouterProvider when present), and veaOutboxProvider for outbox-chain reads. The latter becomes outboxChainProvider in settled-block resolution and is also used to calculate the lookback floor and finalized log-scan head.

Why: veaOutbox.stateRoot({ blockTag }) and Claimed log ranges must use block numbers from the chain hosting veaOutbox, not the router chain.

validator-cli/src/helpers/validator.ts

The old generic queryRpc variable becomes l1Provider for the Arbitrum finality check. Resolution then passes both veaOutboxProvider and optional veaRouterProvider to getClaimResolveState.

The settled-block call intentionally does not pass outboxChainProvider here. This branch consumes only settledBlocks.inboxBlock to read the inbox snapshot; fetching a Chiado finalized head would be dead work.

Why: challenge decisions need a settled Arbitrum snapshot, while the later resolve-state check has distinct outbox-contract and Arbitrum-message-status responsibilities.

validator-cli/src/utils/claim.ts

ClaimResolveStateParams now documents and accepts both provider roles. The outbox provider supplies the outbox finalized head used for claimHashes(epoch, { blockTag }). Message status instead receives veaRouterProvider ?? veaOutboxProvider.

const status = await fetchMessageStatus(
  claimResolveState.sendSnapshot.txHash,
  veaInboxProvider,
  veaRouterProvider ?? veaOutboxProvider
);

Why: the claim hash lives in the Chiado outbox for the routed deployment, but the Arbitrum SDK’s child-to-parent message is resolved against Arbitrum’s Sepolia parent.

validator-cli/src/watcher.ts

The claimer dependency object now includes veaRouterProvider, matching the validator path that already received it.

Why: without this one-line thread-through, production Arbitrum→Gnosis claims would still fall back to the Chiado outbox provider for the Sepolia finality check.

validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.test.ts

Adds a regression test with deliberately different Sepolia and Chiado block numbers. It verifies that finality still uses the Sepolia result while returned outboxBlock comes from outboxChainProvider.getBlock("finalized").

validator-cli/src/utils/claim.test.ts

Adds two role-separation tests: the routed case checks Chiado is used for claimHashes and Sepolia for message status; the non-routed case checks message status falls back to the outbox provider.

Review verdict + residual findings

AcceptNo blocking issue found in the inspected diff.

The provider flow is coherent end to end and matches the stated F2 task. The added tests target the two dangerous boundaries: selecting the outbox-chain block number and selecting the parent provider for Arbitrum message status. git diff --check is clean.

Residual findings
  • Coverage gap, low risk: no new helper/watcher assertion proves that checkAndClaim receives the router provider and forwards the two exact provider objects to resolveSettledReadBlocks. The production wiring is present in the diff, and lower-level role separation is tested.
  • Verification limit: tests were not executed for this report because inspection was restricted to read-only Git operations. The verdict is static-review only.
  • Naming debt, non-blocking: ResolveSettledReadBlocksParams.outboxProvider now means “L1/router finality provider,” while outboxChainProvider means the actual outbox chain. Comments make this accurate, but a future rename to l1Provider would reduce caller confusion.
